T4.2.message: tamas appears only as 'darkness' (en) / 'अन्धकार' (hi), in both meaning and literal. The context points to the inner sense: shlokam-vedasara-shiva-stava.md gives 'beyond all ignorance' (word gloss तमः = ignorance), and gitapress-stotraratnavali.md gives 'अज्ञानसे परे'. The MW gloss recorded in the component (mw-tamas: 'mental darkness, ignorance') supports this too. 'Darkness' can be read as a figure of speech, so this is not clearly wrong. A human should decide whether the contextual meaning should name ignorance and leave the image of darkness in literal.
T4.2.suggested_fix: meaning.en: '(Him, i.e. Śiva,) who is beyond the darkness of ignorance and has no beginning or end'; meaning.hi: 'अज्ञान-रूपी अन्धकार से परे और आदि-अन्त से रहित (शिव)'. Keep literal as is.
